speaker: Unknown
en: Joining us on stage is the co-founder of Instagram and a member of technical staff at Anthropic, Mike Krieger.
zh: 今天登台的嘉宾是 Instagram 联合创始人、Anthropic 技术团队成员 Mike Krieger。

speaker: Unknown
en: How's everyone doing?
zh: 大家最近过得怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: Good morning?
zh: 早上好?

speaker: Unknown
en: Nice.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike, thank you for releasing Fable just in time for us.
zh: Mike,谢谢你正好赶在我们大会之前发布了 Fable。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly for the conference.
zh: 正好赶上这次大会。

speaker: Unknown
en: We timed it.
zh: 我们掐好了时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're so glad to have you.
zh: 我们非常高兴你能来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are one of the preeminent builders, and you're leading labs at Anthropic.
zh: 你是最杰出的构建者之一,而且你在 Anthropic 领导着实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: How has your model usage changed as you've seen models internally grow?
zh: 随着你看到模型在公司内部不断成长,你自己的模型使用方式发生了怎样的变化?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, for me, it's been like both the model shift and then my role shift.
zh: 对我来说,其实既有模型的变化,也有我角色的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for like the first two years I was at Anthropic, I was chief product officer.
zh: 在我加入 Anthropic 的头两年,我是首席产品官。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I kept seeing people build with the models.
zh: 那时我一直看到别人用模型来构建东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the FOMO just kept increasing because I was using the models as much as possible.
zh: 我的 FOMO 越来越强,因为我自己已经尽可能多地使用模型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for example, on product strategy, I would write a strategy doc and then have Claude critique it.
zh: 但比如在产品战略上,我会写一份战略文档,然后让 Claude 来批判它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe you can use a workflow, but it's not quite the same as like building in that pure way.
zh: 也许你可以用某种工作流,但这和那种纯粹的方式构建并不完全一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like spending all my weekends trying to build with it.
zh: 我把所有周末都花在试着用模型构建上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I realized, okay, I actually just need to shift
zh: 然后我意识到,好吧,我其实真的需要转变角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's way too interesting a time.
zh: 这个时代实在太有意思了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's actually an interesting trend I've seen now.
zh: 而且这其实是我如今观察到的一个有趣趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Several people that were CTOs at other places are now joining as ICs at Anthropic in other places.
zh: 好几个曾经在别处担任 CTO 的人,现在以 IC(个人贡献者)的身份加入了 Anthropic 或其他地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I made a role shift, and it was actually right around the time where we started getting internal snapshots of what became Mythos and Fable.
zh: 我做了角色上的转变,而那正好是在我们开始拿到后来成为 Mythos 和 Fable 的内部快照的前后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what was really interesting watching that sort of shift was that
zh: 观察这种转变,真正有意思的地方在于,

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of change between I have an idea, I'm gonna like sort of break it down in my head, much more how I would do engineering normally, and then kind of iterate through these different steps to moving to much more of the paradigm of I'm gonna describe the goal, like go off and work on it, and then like we can talk about what trade-offs you, you know, surface some questions along the way, but then figure out where you landed and where we can go from there.
zh: 从「我有一个想法,我要在脑子里把它拆解」——那更接近我平时做工程的方式——然后逐步迭代不同的步骤,转变为更多的是这样一个范式:我来描述目标,你去干,然后我们可以聊聊你在这个过程中 surfaced 哪些权衡、提出了哪些问题,再看看你落在了哪里,我们从那里接着往前走。

speaker: Unknown
en: I find it's hard, I don't know if people have this experience where
zh: 我觉得这挺难的,不知道大家有没有这样的体验,

speaker: Unknown
en: I know Vable's only been re-enabled for a couple of days.
zh: 我知道 Vable 才重新启用没几天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vable's definitely way, way smarter than me.
zh: Vable 确实比我聪明得多,聪明太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So sometimes it'll finish work and be like, here's the trade-offs I made.
zh: 所以有时候它干完活会说:这是我在权衡中做的取舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, can you explain it to me like I'm a little dumber than you are because I need you to sort of break this down for me?
zh: 我就说:能不能解释得再简单点,就当我比你笨一点,因为我需要你把这个给我拆解一下?

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's been one sort of big change is sort of moving from that task delegation to express the end state and then have it go and cook on it.
zh: 但这是一个很大的变化,就是从那种「任务委派」转变为「表达最终状态」,然后让它自己去搞定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we're all learning how to delegate better.
zh: 是啊,我们都在学习如何更好地委派。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tariq did us a huge favor yesterday.
zh: Tariq 昨天帮了我们一个大忙。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to read it in the newspaper?
zh: 你想在报纸上读到它吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: We have write-ups of talks now in the next day's newspaper.
zh: 我们现在有第二天报纸上的演讲报道。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, be unreasonable.
zh: 他说:要「不合常理」。

speaker: Unknown
en: In what ways have you been more ambitious in your prompting?
zh: 在提示词方面,你在哪些地方变得更雄心勃勃了?

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that.
zh: 我喜欢这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I love that framing.
zh: 我喜欢这个提法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually just hit this today.
zh: 我们今天就刚碰上这种事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the labs initiatives I have is this internal product, and somebody was like, hey, it doesn't work the way I want it to, and can you make some changes?
zh: 我在实验室的举措之一是这个内部产品,有人跟我说:嘿,它没按我想要的方式工作,能不能做些改动?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I realized, oh, I'm just going to go ask Claude to do this.
zh: 我意识到:哦,我直接让 Claude 去做就行了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, why don't you ask Claude?
zh: 就像,你为什么不问问 Claude?

speaker: Unknown
en: And this was a non-technical person.
zh: 而这是一个非技术背景的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually think as an industry or even as a product team,
zh: 所以我真的觉得,作为一个行业,甚至作为一个产品团队,

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to teach people to be more unreasonable in their usage, and it's sort of hard to imagine.
zh: 我们必须教会人们在使⽤上更「不合常理」一些,这其实有点难以想象。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that, if I can digress for a second on product design, I think right now, the kind of first generation of AI products, we put them too much in a box and constrained their sort of access to tools or kind of degrees of freedom, which means it was much harder to be unreasonable, right, when you say,
zh: 我想,如果让我岔开话题聊一下产品设计,我认为现在这一代最早的 AI 产品,我们把它们框得太死了,限制了它们对工具的访问或者说自由度,这意味着要「不合常理」就难得多,对吧,当你说:

speaker: Unknown
en: Do this thing for me, and then it would be like, oh, I can't.
zh: 给我做这件事,然后它会说:哦,我做不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can write code, but I can't really run it, or I can kind of introspect my environment, but not really.
zh: 我能写代码,但我没法真正运行它,或者我勉强能内省我的环境,但也谈不上真正内省。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think as you see our own product progression, even with things like CoWork, where does every single knowledge worker need a virtual machine that can write bash?
zh: 我想看看我们自己的产品演进,即使是像 CoWork 这样的东西——每个知识工作者都需要一台能写 bash 的虚拟机吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: On the face of it, no, but then when you realize, oh, actually, that way it can remediate an issue where, oh, I tried to parse a PDF using our built-in PDF file, so I hit this yesterday, and it was like, oh, I can't parse it this way.
zh: 表面上看,不需要,但当你意识到:哦,其实这样一来它就能补救某个问题——比如我昨天就碰到了,我试着用我们内置的 PDF 工具解析一个 PDF,结果它说:哦,我没法这样解析它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, okay, well, I can probably write a script that can do this as well.
zh: 嗯，好吧，我大概也能写个脚本来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's it.
zh: 所以我觉得就这样吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: My most unreasonable thing, though, was one of our labs projects I wrote in Python, like, near and dear to my heart.
zh: 不过，我最不合理的项目之一，是我们实验室项目之一，我用 Python 写的，这个项目让我特别有感情。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of Instagram is in Python.
zh: 整个 Instagram 都是 Python 写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're finally converting it to PHP now that they have, like, models that can do it.
zh: 我觉得他们现在终于在把它转成 PHP 了，因为他们有了能做到这件事的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, God.
zh: 哦，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know.
zh: 我知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for deployment, I realized that Claude Code had figured out a better deployment story with Bun, and I was like, okay, I need to port this whole thing from Python to TypeScript.
zh: 部署的时候，我发现 Claude Code 用 Bun 找到了更好的部署方案，我就想，好吧，我得把这一整套东西从 Python 迁移到 TypeScript。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I put on my 2010s engineering hat, or even my early 20s, that's a dumb idea.
zh: 如果我戴上 2010 年代的工程师帽子，甚至是 20 年代初的，这都是个蠢主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who would ever port at that point a couple hundred, thousands of lines of code?
zh: 谁会在那个节点去迁移几百、几千行代码呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: But I was like, I think this is doable now, and I basically created this dynamic workflow
zh: 但我想，我觉得现在这是可行的，然后我基本上搭了一个动态工作流

speaker: Unknown
en: Setup, and over the weekend had it port the whole thing, like verify it, double check it, then read both code, like just basically churn and churn and churn, and then came back Monday to a completed workflow that was a ported version of that thing.
zh: 环境，周末就让它把整个东西迁移完了，比如验证、复查，然后两边代码都读，就是不停地运转运转再运转，然后周一回来时就得到一个完成了的工作流，是那个东西迁移好的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that probably ranks on like the more unreasonable things like, yeah, just port this entire Python code base to TypeScript, get it working, get it deployable in, you know, a weekend.
zh: 所以这大概算得上比较不合理的事情之一，比如，是的，把整个 Python 代码库迁移到 TypeScript，让它跑起来，在一个周末就能部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, a lot of people are talking about the BunZig to Rust version.
zh: 是的，很多人都在谈论 Bun 从 Zig 迁到 Rust 的那个版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of people are also like, well, it's a compiler, it's a runtime, it's got lots of tests, easy to do.
zh: 我觉得很多人也会说，好吧，它是个编译器，是个运行时，有大量的测试，容易做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you port Instagram, which you would know very well, to PHP like that, like a product?
zh: 那你能像那样把 Instagram 迁移到 PHP 吗？一个产品，你对它非常了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think the product side, it's even easier or harder.
zh: 是的，我觉得产品这边，甚至更简单或者更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things we did at Instagram, this is when Python 3 came out, and we were able to add type hints for the first time.
zh: 我们在 Instagram 做过一件事，就是 Python 3 刚出来的时候，我们第一次能够添加类型注解。

speaker: Unknown
en: People had a lot of internal conversations, like, are we gonna run out of steam on Python?
zh: 内部有过很多讨论，比如，我们在 Python 上会不会后劲不足？

speaker: Unknown
en: And my perspective was always, like, I think we can take this way further than we think we can, but I think types are gonna help us not sort of be in our own way.
zh: 而我的观点一直是，我觉得我们能走得更远，比我们认为的更远，但我觉得类型能帮我们不至于挡住自己的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we built this thing called MonkeyType, where we basically, like, captured runtime types, like, basically the types that were actually getting used in production, and then mapped those back to the types in the codebase.
zh: 于是我们做了个叫 MonkeyType 的东西，我们基本上是捕获运行时类型，也就是生产环境中实际用到的类型，然后把这些类型映射回代码库。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think...
zh: 然后我觉得……

speaker: Unknown
en: Because of that sort of pattern, I think there's really interesting ways in which if you're doing sort of conversion or sort of cross-compiling using LMs, you can also lean on production data a lot more or run sort of like segmented tests.
zh: 因为那种模式，我觉得用 LLM 做转换或者交叉编译时，有一些非常有趣的方式，你还可以更多地依赖生产数据，或者运行类似分段测试的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that like there's a lot of things you can do there.
zh: 我觉得在那方面可以做的事情很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think it's, I mean, the sky's the limit there as well.
zh: 但是的，我觉得，我的意思是，那里也是天空才是极限。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the hardest part is always finding the boundary around where you can start doing it incrementally without trying to boil the whole ocean and like swap it overnight.
zh: 我觉得最难的部分始终是找到边界，让你可以增量地开始做，而不是试图一口吞下整个海洋，一夜之间全换掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, your users are your tests ultimately.
zh: 我是说，你的用户终究就是你的测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also read another article in the newspaper about how you can just use rollouts.
zh: 我还在报纸上读了另一篇文章，讲你怎么可以使用 rollout。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes you don't really know what you're going to need it for.
zh: 有时候你并不真的知道自己要用它做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when that infrastructure exists for your experiment and to roll things out, it enables so much.
zh: 但当那套基础设施为你的实验和 rollout 而存在时，它能带来太多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I always found, this is advice we got.
zh: 是的，我总是觉得，这是我们得到的一条建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like we launched Instagram and it happened to be the first week everything melted because we didn't really know what we were doing on the backend side of things.
zh: 就是我们上线了 Instagram，结果第一周一切都崩了，因为我们在后端这方面真的不太懂自己在干什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And coincidentally, that week there was like a lunch that one of our investors just scheduled, like not even for us, it was just an infrastructure lunch.
zh: 碰巧那一周，我们的一位投资人安排了一场午餐，甚至都不是为我们安排的，只是一场基础设施午餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we ended up spending, we totally like monopolized that conversation because everybody had their own opinion about how we could fix our scaling.
zh: 结果我们完全垄断了那场对话，因为每个人对我们怎么修复扩容问题都有自己的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like the two pieces of advice I got there is like 2010 that I will forever retain is like basically like
zh: 我在那儿得到的两条建议，2010 年的，我会永远记住，基本上就是

speaker: Unknown
en: Pre-measure everything that you think you might even remotely need because the worst thing is an outage where you're like, well, is this like number normal or is it high?
zh: 提前测量所有你认为哪怕稍微可能需要的东西，因为最糟糕的情况是宕机的时候你在想，这个数字是正常还是偏高？

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, oh, I don't know because I don't have data until I just added this metric.
zh: 然后，哦，我不知道，因为我没有数据，直到我刚加了这个指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other one is being like really thoughtful about knobs and feature flags.
zh: 另一条是，对开关和 feature flag 要非常用心地设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even, you know, early Instagram, we had like a very simple but really effective like way in which you could do like ramp ups and rolls and dynamic config too where, you know,
zh: 所以即使在早期 Instagram，我们就有一套非常简单但非常有效的方式，可以做灰度放量、rollout 和动态配置，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of our runtime configurations had to be changed with a matter of seconds so that we could handle load and being able to do that in a first class way was really important.
zh: 我们的很多运行时配置必须能在几秒钟内更改，这样我们才能应对负载，能以一等公民的方式做到这一点真的非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm seeing that definitely in AI as well where we're making all sorts of different trade-offs and having that kind of runtime configuration is super key.
zh: 我在 AI 领域也肯定看到同样的事，我们在做各种不同的权衡，拥有那种运行时配置超级关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: My favorite scaling story on Instagram, by the way, I think it's like your launch day when you DDoS yourself with email.
zh: 顺便说一句，我在 Instagram 上最喜欢的扩容故事，我觉得是你们上线那天，你们用邮件把自己 DDoS 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which people should look up that story if you haven't seen it.
zh: 如果你还没看过那个故事，应该去查一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to go into tags, very, very major ship.
zh: 我想聊聊 tag，非常、非常重大的一次发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's how 60-something percent of your code is written today.
zh: 如今你 60% 多的代码都是这样写出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you square that with everything you just said, where it's like very dynamic, like you don't actually ship one app, you ship one app with 3,000 flags.
zh: 你怎么把这一点和你刚才说的一切协调起来？就是说非常动态，你实际上发布的不是一个应用，你发布的是带 3000 个 flag 的一个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, well, what are you working on today?
zh: 比如说，你今天在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, like it's for this segment of the population.
zh: 我不知道，就是针对这部分人群的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think there's a bunch of things.
zh: 是，我觉得有很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like with, I was really excited, I was talking to Swix earlier, like I'm really excited that we have tag out there because it is how we've been working for a while and I would get up on stages and people be like, how do you work at Anthropic?
zh: 就像，我之前和 Swix 聊天时非常兴奋，因为我们已经推出了 tag,我真的很兴奋，因为这就是我们一段时间以来的工作方式，我曾站上讲台，人们会问，你们在 Anthropic 是怎么工作的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd be like, oh yeah, we use these things like that are not quite Claude code,
zh: 我会说，哦，我们用的这些东西，不太算是 Claude Code,

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's hard to describe it.
zh: 但很难描述它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you got to poke into Anthropic, you would see, of course, Claude Code usage for things that are more interactive or if you're iterating on a particular specific thing where you want a lot of the high bandwidth back and forth.
zh: 但如果你能潜入 Anthropic 看看，你会看到，当然，对于更交互式的事情，或者当你想针对某个特定的事情进行迭代、需要大量高带宽的来回交流时，会使用 Claude Code。

speaker: Unknown
en: But most usage is actually much more delegating via tagging and via tag.
zh: 但大部分使用实际上更多是通过 tagging 和 tag 来委派。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason it's really interesting is how multiplayer it is.
zh: 而它真正有趣的地方在于它的多人协作性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it reminds me of
zh: 这让我想起

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, mid-journey, the fact that everybody was on Discord, seeing how other people were using it, I think, actually, to your earlier question, really helps with that unreasonableness or ambition, where the first time you see somebody tag Claude and be like, hey, don't just fix this bug, but now you are responsible for this part of the codebase, and I want you to monitor this feedback channel and proactively take on tasks, and then fix them, and then also take, if this API changes, do that.
zh: 实际上是 mid-journey,所有人都在 Discord 上，看到别人怎么使用它，我觉得，回应你之前的问题，这确实有助于那种不合理性或者说雄心，因为你第一次看到有人 tag Claude 并说，嘿，不只是修复这个 bug,而是你现在负责代码库的这一部分，我要你监控这个反馈渠道并主动接手任务，然后修复它们，而且如果这个 API 变了，也要做相应处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw somebody do that, I was like, oh wait, I've been totally underutilizing this thing.
zh: 我看到有人这么做，我就想，哦等等，我一直完全低估了这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've just been using it as like a glorified Claude Code in Slack.
zh: 我只是把它当作 Slack 里一个美化版的 Claude Code 在用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's definitely a totally like sort of new version of it, right?

speaker: Unknown
